name: Investigational varicella vaccine
summary: GSK's varicella new strain (VNS) vaccine is a live attenuated chickenpox vaccine for the routine two-dose childhood schedule. It is in Phase 3 against Merck's Varivax, which with ProQuad is the only varicella-containing vaccine sold in the US. GSK's Varilrix is not US-licensed. The Phase 3 trials in the context file are NCT06693895 (safety, 750 children aged 12 to 15 months, primary completion 2026-11-23) and NCT06806137 (second dose 3 months after the first, 600 children, 2026-12-14). The price anchor is Varivax at its CDC private-sector price of $192.115 a dose, $384.23 for a two-dose course. The net price blends in the Vaccines for Children federal price. The uptake anchor is GSK's own Priorix, which entered Merck's US MMR monopoly in 2022 and in FY2025 held 2.7% of the US MMR, MMRV and varicella revenue pool.

therapy_mode.source: ACIP routine schedule: two varicella doses, at 12 to 15 months and 4 to 6 years. NCT06806137 tests a second dose after a first at 12 to 15 months
therapy_mode.note: One course per child on an annual birth cohort, billed once. The book models its pediatric vaccines this way (sny_pcv21.csv, gsk_mrna_seasonal_flu.csv). The second dose falls about three years after the first, so the engine books it early

list_price_per_patient.source: Varivax (Merck), CDC Pediatric/VFC Vaccine Price List of January 2026 (https://www.cdc.gov/vaccines-for-children/media/pdfs/2026/01/Pediatric-VFC-Vaccine-Price-List-01-26-26.pdf): private sector $192.115 a dose, contract to 6/30/2026. Two doses = $384.23
list_price_per_patient.note: JUDGEMENT on the course. The comparator is Varivax, the standalone varicella vaccine this asset is tested against. The April 2026 list (contract to 3/31/2027) reads $191.365 private, per a search summary; the PDF itself was not opened. In GBP, the currency of the book's GSK seeds: $384.23 at 1.327632 = GBP 289.41 (0.00028941 mm GBP). CMS has no usable figure: Proquad Part D 2024 is 38 beneficiaries at $258 (lookup.py demand), and Varivax has no row. The case against: many US children get their second dose as ProQuad (MMRV, private $289.168 on the January list). GSK has no US MMRV, so where ProQuad takes dose two, GSK sells one dose, $192, not two

gross_to_net_pct.source: Vaccines for Children blend, the method sny_pcv21.csv uses: 52.2% of US children are VFC-eligible (MMWR 2024;73(33), as cited in that seed) and are supplied at the CDC contract price of $115.067 against $192.115 private (January 2026 list). 0.522 x 115.067 + 0.478 x 192.115 = $151.90, 79.07% of list, so 20.93% comes off
gross_to_net_pct.note: JUDGEMENT on the list edition. A search summary of the April 2026 list gives a CDC price of $158.98 against $191.365 private, which would make it 8.8% off. That figure is unconfirmed, so the January pair, both read from one list, is used. The VFC share counts eligible children, not doses drawn. The house Part D convention of 0.5 does not apply to a CDC-contracted pediatric vaccine

discontinuation_pct.unit: share of the treated stock stopping per year
discontinuation_pct.source: one course, not repeated: routine varicella vaccination has no booster after the two doses (ACIP schedule)
discontinuation_pct.note: No patient is billed a second year. Stated so the engine never carries a stock forward, whichever mode reads it

forecast_start_year.source: Phase 3 primary completions 2026-11-23 (NCT06693895) and 2026-12-14 (NCT06806137); the lot-consistency study NCT06740630 against Varivax completes 2026-12-25 (ClinicalTrials.gov, via search)
forecast_start_year.note: JUDGEMENT. A BLA filed during 2027 and a standard review put approval in 2028. An ACIP vote and a CDC contract are needed before VFC volume, so 2029 is the first full year, later than the 2027 default. No filing date is published. The case against: an early-2027 filing could make 2028 a full year

exus_multiple.source: Merck ProQuad / M-M-R II / Varivax, FY2025: $566mm outside the US against $1,885mm in the US (asset_revenue_regions, sec_fsds, Merck 10-K 0000310158-26-000063)
exus_multiple.note: JUDGEMENT, and possibly too high. It is the comparator's split, but ex-US GSK already sells Varilrix and Priorix-Tetra (GBP 122mm Europe and GBP 162mm International in FY2025 per a search summary of GSK's FY2025 results), so a new strain would largely replace its own product there. Incremental ex-US revenue could be near zero

economics_share.source: GSK Q1 2026 pipeline report (https://www.gsk.com/media/40yljs4u/q1-2026-pipeline-assets-and-clinical-trials-report.pdf) lists it as a GSK asset. GlaxoSmithKline is sole lead sponsor on both Phase 3 records
economics_share.note: No partner or royalty was found

prevalence.source: US births in 2024, National Vital Statistics Reports 75-02, Births: Final Data for 2024, the figure sny_pcv21.csv carries
prevalence.note: lookup.py pool Chickenpox and Varicella return nothing, so the book carries no pool for this disease. The birth cohort is the same count the book uses for pneumococcal disease, since a routine childhood vaccine's pool is the cohort, not cases

incidence.source: stated equal to prevalence: a new cohort arrives every year and the last one ages out of the schedule
incidence.note: The engine's carryover-zero shape, as for PCV21. The peak is then the share of each year's cohort vaccinated with this product

eligible_pct.source: MMWR 2026;75(11):146-155, Vaccination Coverage by Age 24 Months Among Children Born in 2021 and 2022 (NIS-Child 2022-2024): 90.0% received at least one varicella dose
eligible_pct.note: One-dose coverage by 24 months. Two-dose completion comes later and is lower, so pricing every eligible child at two doses leans high

penetration_peak_pct.unit: share of the eligible cohort's courses per year
penetration_peak_pct.source: GSK's own Priorix, the one measured entry into a Merck childhood MMR/V monopoly: US sales of Priorix, Priorix Tetra and Varilrix of GBP 39mm in FY2025 (GSK FY2025 results announcement, 4 February 2026, per a search summary, not opened), $51.8mm at 1.327632, against Merck's US ProQuad / M-M-R II / Varivax of $1,885mm (asset_revenue_regions). 51.8 / (1,885 + 51.8) = 2.67%
penetration_peak_pct.note: JUDGEMENT, at a 1.0 multiple and taken as the plateau. Value share of the whole MMR/V pool stands in for course share. The case for more: Priorix competes only with M-M-R II, so its share of that segment is higher; 2025 was its third full year after June 2022 approval, and US sales more than doubled. Solved through the curve below as still ramping (s-curve at index 2 is 35.6% of peak), the peak would be 0.075. The case for less: H1 2025 US sales were GBP 33mm of the GBP 39mm full year, which looks like outbreak-driven stocking in the 2025 measles year, not a run rate; and ProQuad takes many second doses

ramp_steepness.source: reused from sny_pcv21.csv: the lower-quartile fit over the 41 measured launches in data/launch_ramp.csv, taken for a pediatric birth-cohort market
ramp_steepness.note: No CMS series exists for a pediatric vaccine, and Priorix's US revenue has only three full years on file

ramp_midpoint_year.source: reused from sny_pcv21.csv, fitted with the steepness above
ramp_midpoint_year.note: Half the peak by late 2031, which lets an ACIP recommendation and the CDC contract cycle take effect
